Margins
How to read this: Distribution is measured as AP (Accounts Purchasing) — distinct buying accounts — at four windows: lifetime (Total), trailing 12 months (1YR), trailing 6 months (6M), and an approximate trailing 90 days (3 calendar months, since the source data is monthly rather than daily). Margins are realized figures — Unit Price minus Laid-in Cost, weighted by units actually sold — computed from real invoice transactions, not a theoretical price sheet, since we only have full FOB/Tax/Distrib-Allowance cost detail for a single sample item. Invoice rows with both $0 Unit Price and $0 Ext Price (bulk same-day batches with no revenue — load-sheet/inventory movements, not paid sales) are excluded from the Margins tab so they don't distort margin %. Every number here covers the full W&S portfolio, not just a few example brands.

Brand by Item — Distribution (Accounts Purchasing)

What do these columns mean?
Total AP
Lifetime distinct buying accounts for this item, across every month in the data (2025/1 through the latest month).
1YR AP
Distinct buying accounts in the trailing 12 complete months.
6M AP
Distinct buying accounts in the trailing 6 complete months.
90D AP
Distinct buying accounts in the trailing ~90 days, approximated as the last 3 calendar months (source data is monthly).
Trend
Compares the current 90D AP window to the 3 months immediately before it. Up = gaining buyers, Down = losing buyers, Flat = unchanged.
FY25 / FY26 Buyers
Full calendar-year 2025 buyer count vs. year-to-date 2026 — a full year vs. a partial year, so treat the comparison directionally.

Realized Margins by Item

What do these columns mean?
Avg Unit Price
Total $Vol (sum of Ext Price) divided by units sold — the actual net price achieved, after any discounts.
Avg Laid-In Cost
Weighted average landed cost per unit (FOB + freight + duties, as recorded in Encompass), before any distributor margin.
Margin $/Unit
Avg Unit Price minus Avg Laid-In Cost.
Margin %
Margin $/Unit divided by Avg Unit Price.
Avg Discount/Unit
Average per-unit discount off full price, for context on how much margin is being given up in deals.
